title: A Compact 10b Source Driver IC with Delta-Sigma Pulse Width Modulation for Low-Voltage Digital Interpolation Achieving 1884μm2/Channel
problem: High-resolution mobile displays require more source-driver channels, increasing silicon area and cost. Conventional interpolation sub-DAC topologies (Gm-adjustment, switched-capacitor, charge-modulation) suffer from inherent nonlinearity (Gm methods) or require additional capacitors/high-voltage devices that increase channel area.
motivation: Mobile gaming and 3D rendering drive higher display resolution; channel area directly impacts SoC cost and die size, making compact channel design critical.
method: A 10-bit compact source-driver IC uses delta-sigma pulse-width-modulation (SD-PWM) for low-voltage digital interpolation between gamma voltages. SD-PWM replaces analog interpolation circuits with digital modulation, reducing capacitor and transistor overhead while maintaining linearity.
key_novelty: Delta-sigma PWM interpolation enables compact low-voltage DAC without capacitors or high-voltage blocks, achieving 1884μm²/channel.
contributions: Delta-sigma PWM interpolation for low-voltage DAC in source drivers
Compact 10-bit resolution without additional capacitors or HV devices
1884 μm²/channel area—significant reduction vs. prior interpolation methods
Suitable for high-resolution mobile OLED/LCD displays
primary_theme: Compact SD-PWM source-driver IC for high-resolution displays
